title: Ngorongoro Crater Lodges: Where to Stay on the Rim, in the Highlands and in Karatu
meta_title: Ngorongoro Crater Lodges: 7 Best Places to Stay
meta_description: Ngorongoro crater lodges compared: rim vs highlands vs Karatu, which lodges are open, nightly fees and who each stay suits.
excerpt: The best Ngorongoro crater lodges compared by area, style and budget: rim lodges for views and early starts, highland camps for walks and Karatu farm stays for value, plus the fees that change the maths.
content:
The best Ngorongoro crater lodges sit right on the crater rim, with views 600 metres down to the floor, while good-value alternatives lie in the farmland around Karatu, about 30 minutes from the park gate. Choose the rim for early game drives and views, the highlands for walks, or Karatu for value and warmth.

Picking a base is harder than it looks. Rim stays add nightly fees, two famous names are closed for rebuilding, and the side of the rim changes how fast you reach the floor. This guide compares the main options by area, style and budget, and shows who each one suits.

Quick Facts

  • Where to stay: on the crater rim, in the Olmoti highlands or in Karatu outside the conservation area
  • Crater: the world's largest unbroken caldera, about 610 metres deep and listed by UNESCO since 1979
  • Karatu to the gate: about 15 km, or around 30 minutes, to Loduare Gate; allow about another hour to the crater descent
  • Arusha to Karatu: about 140 km on tarmac, roughly 3 hours by road
  • Key fees: US$70.80 entry per 24 hours, US$59 nightly concession fee inside the area, US$295 per vehicle per crater descent (checked October 2026)
  • Nights needed: one night for most itineraries, two or three for walks and highland craters
  • Pack: a warm fleece and jacket, as rim nights are cold all year

Where Are the Ngorongoro Crater Lodges?

Ngorongoro crater lodges fall into three zones: the crater rim itself, the wider highlands around Olmoti Crater, and the town of Karatu just outside the conservation area. No accommodation is allowed on the crater floor, so every guest drives down by 4x4 for the day and climbs back out in the afternoon.

The crater is a collapsed volcano whose walls rise about 610 metres above the floor. Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim sit inside the conservation area, so you pay conservation fees for every 24 hours you stay. Karatu lies outside the boundary among coffee farms, on the main road from Arusha.

The western rim versus the eastern rim

Most Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim are on the western and south-western side, close to Loduare Gate and the Seneto descent road, which is the busiest route onto the floor. The eastern rim is quieter and sits beside the Lemala access road. Lemala Ngorongoro says its guests usually gain about an hour on vehicles using the Seneto road, which matters if you want the floor before the main crowds arrive.

Rim, Highlands or Karatu: Which Is Best?

The best base among Ngorongoro crater lodges depends on your priorities. The rim suits travellers who want views and an early crater start, the highlands suit walkers and repeat visitors, and Karatu suits families, budget-conscious travellers and anyone who finds altitude cold.

ZoneBest forTrade-offsTime to the crater floor
Crater rimViews from your room, early game drives, a short first-time stayCold nights, nightly conservation and concession fees, fewer budget optionsShortest: Lemala guests can be on the floor within 10-15 minutes
Olmoti highlandsForest walks, Olmoti and Empakaai crater hikes, privacyFurther from the crater, high and cool, best with two or three nightsAbout 1 hour to the crater
KaratuValue, warmer nights, gardens and farm settings, familiesLonger morning drive, crater views only from the rim roadAbout 30 minutes to Loduare Gate, then about 1 hour to the descent

Many itineraries combine two zones: a night in Karatu after Lake Manyara or Tarangire, then a night on the rim before the crater drive and onwards to the Serengeti. Our Tanzania northern circuit itinerary shows how the crater fits between the other parks.

Best Ngorongoro Crater Lodges on the Rim

The rim is where the classic Ngorongoro crater lodges stand, with views across the caldera from rooms, decks and dining areas. These four rim properties are open and taking bookings, and each has a different style, from a large stone lodge to a 10-tent camp in old acacia forest.

Ngorongoro Serena Safari Lodge

Ngorongoro Serena Safari Lodge is built from river stone and draped in indigenous vines, with arched passages and timbered decks along the rim. It has 74 rooms and a suite, each with a private stone balcony facing the crater. There is a spa, and guided nature walks run morning and evening. It suits first-time visitors who want a classic, full-service choice among Ngorongoro crater lodges, with crater views from every room.

Ngorongoro Lodge Meliá Collection

Ngorongoro Lodge Meliá Collection is the most hotel-like of the Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim, with rim rooms, family rooms and a long list of suites, plus a heated pool, spa and butler service, and most rooms face the crater. It suits families and travellers who want resort comforts at the end of a game drive.

Lemala Ngorongoro Tented Camp

Lemala Ngorongoro Tented Camp has 10 spacious tents in an ancient acacia forest on the eastern rim, next to the Lemala access road. Game drives can leave at 6:15am and reach the floor within 10 to 15 minutes. One tent has two bedrooms. Among Ngorongoro crater lodges it suits photographers, couples and small groups who prefer canvas to concrete.

Entamanu Ngorongoro

Entamanu Ngorongoro, run by Nomad Tanzania, sits on the wilder side of the rim in Maasai grazing land, with cottage-style rooms raised on wooden platforms and two family tents. From camp you look into the crater on one side and towards the Serengeti plains on the other. Rim walks with a Maasai guide are a highlight. Its sister camp, Entamanu Private, sits on the remote north-western rim for groups wanting privacy.

Which Ngorongoro Crater Lodges Are Closed or Coming Soon?

Two well-known Ngorongoro crater lodges are not taking guests right now, and older guides still list them as open. Check status before you book, because closed lodges often appear in older itineraries.

andBeyond Ngorongoro Crater Lodge closed in January 2025 for a full refurbishment and is not expected to reopen before early 2027. The former Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge on the north-eastern rim is being redeveloped by Elewana as Ngorongoro Explorer, which the company says will open in June 2027.

Where to Stay in the Ngorongoro Highlands

The highlands beyond the classic Ngorongoro crater lodges suit travellers who want more than a single crater drive. The Highlands, run by Asilia on the slopes of Olmoti Crater, is the standout option, which Asilia describes as the highest-elevation camp in the region, about an hour's drive from the Ngorongoro Crater.

The Highlands has eight canvas-and-perspex domed suites with wood-burning stoves, including a family suite and a honeymoon suite with an outdoor hot tub. Guided hikes to Olmoti Crater and to Empakaai Crater, with its flamingo-lined soda lake, are open to guests aged 12 and over. Asilia lists rates from US$710 per person per night in April and May 2026, rising to US$1,390 from June to October 2026, and recommends three nights for Empakaai.

Best Lodges in Karatu Near the Crater

Karatu is the smart alternative to Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim if you want comfort and value without paying nightly conservation and concession fees. The town sits about 15 km, or roughly 30 minutes, from Loduare Gate. Two historic farm lodges stand out.

Gibb's Farm

Gibb's Farm is a working coffee farm on the outer slopes of the Ngorongoro highlands, founded as a coffee plantation in the 1920s and overlooking the Great Rift Valley. Guests stay in themed cottages, eat organic food grown on the farm and can join farm walks and coffee tastings. It suits food lovers, families and anyone wanting a slower pace between parks.

The Manor at Ngorongoro

The Manor at Ngorongoro, part of the Elewana Collection, is a Cape Dutch-style manor house set on a 1,500-acre Arabica coffee estate next to the conservation area. It has nine cottages holding 18 suites, plus a family cottage. White gabled buildings, mature gardens and fine dining suit honeymoons and special occasions, with the crater an easy day trip away.

Budget alternatives to Ngorongoro crater lodges

Budget travellers usually skip Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim, stay in one of Karatu's simpler lodges and drive up for the day. Camping on the rim is another option at US$35.40 per adult per night on top of entry fees (checked October 2026). Our Tanzania safari on a budget guide covers more ways to save.

How Much Do Ngorongoro Crater Lodges Cost?

Ngorongoro crater lodges range from simple Karatu lodges at the budget end to rim and highland camps where peak-season rates can pass US$1,000 per person per night, as The Highlands' do. Lodge rates are only part of the cost, because the conservation area charges entry, concession and crater fees that apply to everyone.

The fees below come from the Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority tariffs for non-resident adults (checked October 2026). Tariffs can change without notice, so confirm them before you book.

FeeAmount (non-resident adult)When you pay it
Conservation area entryUS$70.80 per personFor every 24 hours inside the conservation area
Lodge or permanent camp concession feeUS$59 per person per nightEach night at a lodge or camp inside the conservation area
Crater service feeUS$295 per vehicleEach time your vehicle descends to the crater floor
Public campsiteUS$35.40 per person per nightEach night camping on the rim

The concession fee is the hidden difference. A couple spending a night on the rim pays US$118 in concession fees on top of entry, and longer stays add a fresh entry fee every 24 hours. Based in Karatu, they pay entry only for their crater visit.

When you compare Ngorongoro crater lodges, ask whether each quote is full board or fully inclusive and whether fees are included. Rates can roughly double between the April-May green season and the June-October peak, as the Asilia figures above show.

When Is the Best Time to Stay at the Ngorongoro Crater?

The Ngorongoro Crater is good all year because its resident wildlife does not migrate, so the best time depends on budget and crowds. June to October is dry, clear and busiest, and Ngorongoro crater lodges charge their highest rates. April and May bring rain, green scenery, fewer vehicles and the lowest prices at many lodges.

Whatever the month, nights at Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim are cold, so lodges supply heaters, stoves or hot-water bottles. Read our Tanzania safari packing checklist before you fly. For a month-by-month view of the wider region, see our guide to the best time to visit Tanzania.

Whichever of the Ngorongoro crater lodges you choose, the floor rewards an early start. The floor has around 120 km of game-drive tracks, and black rhino, lion, hyena, elephant and huge herds of zebra and wildebeest live there all year. Our guide to Ngorongoro Crater wildlife explains what you can expect to see.

Insider Tips

  • Book early for July to October: small Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim fill months ahead
  • Match the rim to your route: western rim for Karatu and Serengeti links, eastern rim for a quieter early descent
  • Check what is open: closed or rebuilding lodges still appear in older itineraries
  • Ask about fees: confirm whether conservation and concession fees are inside or outside each quote
  • Pack for cold: a fleece, warm jacket and hat for evenings and pre-dawn starts on the rim
  • Take a picnic: a packed lunch on the floor lets you stay longer instead of driving back up

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it better to stay on the Ngorongoro Crater rim or in Karatu?

Stay on the rim for an early start on the crater floor and views from your room, or in Karatu for value and warmer nights. Ngorongoro crater lodges on the rim add nightly conservation and concession fees, while Karatu sits outside the conservation area, about 30 minutes from Loduare Gate.

How many nights should I spend at the Ngorongoro Crater?

One night is enough for most travellers, because a single crater game drive of half a day covers the floor well. Two nights suit you if you want a rim walk, a Maasai village visit or a relaxed day after the Serengeti. Three nights at a highland camp such as The Highlands are worthwhile for hikes to Olmoti or Empakaai craters.

Are there any lodges inside the Ngorongoro Crater?

No, there are no lodges on the Ngorongoro Crater floor. All Ngorongoro crater lodges and camps sit on the rim, in the surrounding highlands or outside the conservation area around Karatu. Visitors drive down for the day in a 4x4 vehicle, since only four-wheel-drive vehicles may enter the crater and walking is not allowed on the floor.

Which side of the Ngorongoro Crater rim is best to stay on?

No side is best for everyone. The western and south-western rim is closest to Loduare Gate and the Seneto descent road, which suits travellers coming from Karatu or going on to the Serengeti. The eastern rim near the Lemala road is quieter and can give you a head start on the floor, which suits photographers and early risers.

How much are the fees for staying at the Ngorongoro Crater?

A non-resident adult pays US$70.80 per 24 hours to enter the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, plus US$59 per night as a lodge concession fee when staying inside it, and US$295 per vehicle for each crater descent (checked October 2026). Most Ngorongoro crater lodges include these fees only in full-board packages, so confirm before booking.

Final Thoughts

The right Ngorongoro crater lodges come down to three choices: the rim for views and early starts, the Olmoti highlands for walks, or Karatu for value and warmth. Check that your lodge is open, understand the fees, and match the side of the rim to your route.
